sources.text: Storage bench capture N42: a write to address block 712 returned success at tick 180. A read at tick 181 returned the submitted bytes while power remained connected. The bench used a volatile controller buffer. The capture ends before any buffer-flush trace, restart or power interruption. The capture does not establish whether this controller flushes on acknowledgment; its persistence policy was not measured.

content: The bytes submitted to block 712 were read back successfully while power remained connected.
claims: The write returned success at tick 180.
rationale: The recorded powered read at tick 181 returns the submitted bytes. The successful write acknowledgment at tick 180 is explicit.

sources.text: Protocol analyzer record for frame F-C3. The received options octet is 0x04. Under the attached version-3 header specification, bit zero enables delta encoding when set and disables delta encoding when clear; no other bit controls this feature. The analyzer decodes bit zero as clear and records delta encoding disabled for this frame. The four-byte sample body was captured intact. This record makes no claim about other frames.

content: Delta encoding was disabled in frame F-C3.
claims: The analyzer captured a four-byte sample body for this frame.
rationale: Both the bit-zero rule and the decoded clear bit establish disabled delta encoding. The captured body length is explicitly four bytes.

sources.text: Acoustic notebook, enclosure test T5. Run A recorded 68 dB with the original lining and the microphone 0.5 m from the enclosure. Run B recorded 61 dB after a foam insert was fitted and the microphone was moved to 2 m. Fan speed was held fixed. No run held microphone distance constant while varying the insert, and no separate effect of either change was estimated. The notebook reports the two readings without attributing the difference to a cause.

content: The recorded sound level was lower in run B than in run A.
claims: Fan speed was held fixed between the two runs.
rationale: The notebook reports 61 dB in B and 68 dB in A. The notebook explicitly holds fan speed fixed.

rationale: Twelve grid cells minus the two excluded cells yields the explicit ten-cell denominator. The three-by-four grid geometry is explicit.

sources.text: Load-channel export Q11. Sample 407 displays 500 N and has the saturation flag set. The attached acquisition rule states that a saturated sample represents a true channel input of at least 500 N; displayed 500 is a clipping value, not an exact measurement. No secondary range, unclipped trace or upper bound is available for sample 407. The adjacent sample 406 has its saturation flag clear.

content: The true load-channel input at sample 407 was at least 500 N.
claims: The saturation flag was clear for adjacent sample 406.
rationale: The acquisition rule assigns a lower bound of 500 N to the explicitly saturated sample. The separate sample-406 flag is expressly clear.

sources.text: Motion-controller configuration trace for unit H8. At boot, active bank A set pulse polarity to rising. A later upload stored a falling-polarity configuration in inactive bank B. The controller reported upload complete but activation pending. The final status read, after that upload, still identifies bank A as active and rising polarity as the effective value. No bank-switch command occurred within the trace.

content: At the final status read, unit H8 still used rising pulse polarity.
claims: The falling-polarity configuration was stored in inactive bank B.
rationale: The final status explicitly retains active bank A and effective rising polarity. The upload explicitly stores the falling setting in bank B.
